text:
Sam (runtime): quick heads-up — canary showed tenant-level starvation when long-sequence requests mix with lots of short ones. noticed long tails and KV-hit rate drop for the same tenant.
Ria: ugh — any easy repro? are we seeing mini-batcher ejecting long requests or just delaying them?
Sam (runtime): looks like both. the batcher forms mixed batches, but token-budget targeting skews credits toward short sequences because they complete faster, so long sequences get incremental credits and often get pushed behind. KV warmups then miss and kernel selection flips to slower path. snippet from perf trace: 
```
batch_id=3421 spans=4,avg_seq=12/120,kv_hits=0.12,kernel=fp16_slow,tail_ms=420
batch_id=3422 spans=20,avg_seq=3/8,kv_hits=0.78,kernel=fastpath,tail_ms=34
```
Oliver: hmm that kv_hits drop is the killer. if long sequences get cold KV they pay huge latency tax. are we leaking credits back into the global pool?
Sam (runtime): current refill: per-tenant queue gets credits proportional to recent throughput. short-dominant tenants end up hogging refill cycles. we also have a micro-batcher window that tries to keep latency SLO but doesn't enforce minimum reserve for long sequences.
Marta: proposal — reserve a small sliding token reserve per tenant for sequences > threshold (e.g., seq_len > 64). that reserve should be consumed from the tenant bucket, not the short-path queue. failsafe: if reserve unused for N seconds, it decays.
Ria: sounds ok. metrics to add: tenant_starve_rate, kv_warmup_ratio, kernel_switch_rate. also need per-tenant long/short queue lengths in tracing.
Oliver: alternative approach — batch formation bias: when forming a batch, prefer grouping by estimated remaining tokens instead of by arrival only. so long/long and short/short cluster. cheap heuristic: sort waiting requests by remaining_tokens and allow a small reordering window (20ms).
Sam (runtime): love the reorder window idea. tradeoff is latency for short requests — but we can cap reorder to small fraction. we should A/B both: reserve + reorder.
perf-ci-bot: perf run queued: mini-batcher-reserve-experiment. expect ~30m for baseline + 2 experiments.
Marta: for reserve math: target = max(ceil(0.05 * tenant_token_budget), 8) tokens, refill_rate unchanged but separate bucket. small tenants get floor(4).
Ria: and add a quick toggle: feature flag runtime.enable_mini_reserve. can we also add a metric: reserve_consumption_ratio to know if reserve is starving others?
Sam (runtime): yes. plan:
- implement reserve bucket + decay (PR in next 6h)
- implement sort-by-remaining-token window (PR following day)
- add telemetry: tenant_starve_rate, kv_warmup_ratio, reserve_consumption_ratio, kernel_switch_rate
- run perf-ci experiments and push canary to one rack (no global rollout)
Oliver: suggestion: when reserve triggers, prefer kernel hint to keep KV alive (e.g., mark as warm candidate) — helps avoid the cold->slowpath flip. small code idea: 
```
if (reserve_used) mark_kv_prefetch(batch.tenant)
```
Marta: also add alert if tenant_starve_rate > 0.02 for 5m on canary. prevents regressions.
Ria: who owns the dashboard? I'll wire up grafana panels once perf-ci data lands.
Sam (runtime): I'll open the PR for reserve and add the feature flag. attaching quick config example: 
```yaml
runtime:
  batching:
    reorder_window_ms: 20
    enable_mini_reserve: true
    mini_reserve:
      min_tokens: 4
      pct_of_budget: 0.05
      decay_s: 120
```
perf-ci-bot: experiment started: mini-batcher-reserve-experiment -> baseline, reserve-a, reorder-b. job id 20240514-88.
Oliver: cool. one more ask — add a tiny unit-test that simulates 80% short traffic + 20% long and asserts long median latency doesn't regress > x2.
Sam (runtime): noted. will add smoke simulation in batcher_test.go. aiming to roll out canary by EOD if experiments look sane.
Marta: if canary passes, we should plan a staged rollout with telemetry gating (5 racks -> 20 racks -> all).
Ria: thanks — keep updates in this thread. i'll start the dashboard and alert PR. :thumbsup:
Sam (runtime): thanks team. ping me on pager if any canary alerts fire.
perf-ci-bot: experiment completed: baseline vs reserve-a vs reorder-b. results uploaded to https://perf.redwood.local/exp/20240514-88 (summary pending).
